title: Tor-independent localized comparison for an A-K-flat complex
statement: Let R,A,B,D be commutative rings, with R-algebra structures on A and B, and an E=A\otimes_R B-algebra structure on D. Assume \operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)=0 for every i>0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let Q be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] that is K-flat over A, meaning that its total tensor with every acyclic A-complex is acyclic [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Assume D is flat over E [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every base-derived tensor cohomology model M [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], its specified canonical map D\otimes_E H^i(Q\otimes_R^L B)\to H^i(D\otimes_A Q) is an isomorphism for every i\in\mathbf Z. No boundedness or finiteness of Q, or flatness of A or B over R, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change, Tor-independent affine calculation; More on Algebra, Section 06Y5 and Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above projective resolution F of B[0] over R. The augmentation A tensor_R F -> (A tensor_R B)[0] has positive cohomology zero, degree-zero cohomology E=A tensor_R B, and cohomology in degree -i equal to Tor_i^R(A,B). Resolving B computes Tor in the second variable; tensor symmetry and balancedness identify this with the stated Tor in the first variable. Balancedness follows by resolving both modules projectively and using the two filtrations of the double tensor complex, whose diagonals are finite because both resolutions are bounded above. The Tor hypothesis therefore says that this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism of A-complexes. Bounded-above projective resolutions are R-K-flat.

Tensor that augmentation with the A-K-flat Q over A. Its cone is acyclic, so its total tensor with Q is acyclic by K-flatness. Since total tensor commutes with cones, the tensor augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The mixed tensor associator identifies the source with Tot(Q tensor_R F) and target with Q tensor_A E = Q tensor_R B. The map is the augmentation induced by F -> B[0], including the signed total differentials.

R-K-flatness of F allows the balanced model to compute Q tensor_R^L B by Tot(Q tensor_R F); no R-K-flatness of Q is asserted. The canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison is the augmentation in the preceding step, because both are induced by F -> B[0]. Naturality for multiplication by A and by B makes its cohomology map E-linear. For any stipulated model, comparison_eq identifies the restricted comparison with the universal counit on cohomology, and cohomologyIso_smul fixes the A-action. The balanced comparison, compatible with the same counit and coefficient actions, therefore identifies comparison with that augmentation. Restriction to B-modules reflects isomorphisms, so comparison is an E-module isomorphism.

Flatness of D over E makes scalar extension preserve the cycles, boundaries, and quotient exact sequences, giving the canonical cohomology isomorphism. Ordinary tensor associativity identifies D tensor_E (E tensor_A Q) with D tensor_A Q. Its elementary-tensor map is ordinaryToLocalized_tmul. localized_eq and the extension/restriction adjunction identify localizedComparison with extension of comparison followed by this cohomology isomorphism and associativity. All factors are invertible. The cone argument works for unbounded Q and zero complexes and rings.

theorem localizedComparison_isIso_of_torIndependent_kFlat
    {R A B D : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing D]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra (A ⊗[R] B) D]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (hTor : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((CategoryTheory.Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R A)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R B)))
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ, L.Acyclic →
      (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor L Q (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _)).Acyclic)
    (hD : Module.Flat (A ⊗[R] B) D)
    (M : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (M.localizedComparison i)
